exposure: Maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in late pregnancy
outcome: Neonatal systemic SARS-CoV-2 IgG, IgA, and IgM antibodies in serum
Neonatal mucosal SARS-CoV-2 spike-specific antibodies in saliva
Maternal spike-specific antibodies in serum and breastmilk
Antigen-antibody spike IgA immune complexes in breastmilk
cohort: The study included 28 mother-infant dyads where pregnant women tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection and gave birth at Policlinico Umberto I in Rome, Italy.
finding: Infants fed breastmilk showed significantly increased SARS-CoV-2 spike protein-specific salivary IgA antibodies compared to infants fed an exclusive formula diet, suggesting breastmilk not only provides passive protection but also actively stimulates the neonatal immune system.
